shots.name: Left Orbit
shots.notes: Outermost left lane; wraps up behind the house to the hidden top area. Route to the Back Door.

shots.name: Left Ramp
shots.notes: Wireform ramp with a Scared-Stiff-style crate diverter that can divert into the Trunk lock. Lights Haunts; alternating L/R ramps builds shot multipliers. Backhandable.

shots.name: Junk in the Trunk (Trunk Lock)
shots.notes: Motorized steamer-trunk ball lock, upper-left. Locks balls for Trunk Multiball and awards random Junk pieces.

shots.name: Trunk Targets (36-24-36)
shots.notes: Vertical bank of 3 round standups; completing them opens the trunk lid and helps arm Double Trouble.

shots.name: Garage
shots.notes: Ball-lock scoop guarded by the gravestone drop target; used for the three Garage Multiballs and to access the Cellar.

shots.name: Gravestone Drop Target
shots.notes: Single headstone drop standing in front of the Garage entrance; knock it down to light Garage locks.

shots.name: Mansion Entrance / House
shots.notes: Center staircase into the House bash toy — the primary start/collect shot. Front-door staircase lifts to reveal the Cellar.

shots.name: Cellar
shots.notes: Inner shot revealed under the lifted front-door staircase; finishes many Haunts and is the Gappa Angry / Wild Market Value climax shot.

shots.name: Spinning Attic Turret
shots.notes: Motorized eyeball attic turret atop the House; rotates during House Party (hit House when the eye faces you to add a ball).

shots.name: Super Secret Back Door
shots.notes: Rear-of-house opening reached via a soft plunge / left orbit; unskilled skill shot that qualifies/advances a Haunt.

shots.name: Right Ramp
shots.notes: Ramp right of the House; returns safely to the flippers. Alternating L/R ramps builds shot multipliers. Backhandable.

shots.name: Deadhead Family Crypt
shots.notes: Green mausoleum bash-toy + scoop (Crypt Kicker). Deadhead skull is the bash target; the Crypt Cleaner battle track and a multiball lock.

shots.name: Right Orbit
shots.notes: Outermost right lane; wraps to the hidden top area. Carries the Beast Booster spinner.

shots.name: Beast Booster Spinner
shots.notes: Opto spinner over the right orbit; raises base values (used in Teenagers from Outer Space).

shots.name: Gar-Goil Targets
shots.notes: Row of green interactive standups; build the Garg-Oil-Gauge to start Gar-Goils Gone Wild.

shots.name: Hand of Fate Targets
shots.notes: Three red standups; complete to light the Hand of Fate wheel at the left outlane and help arm Double Trouble.

shots.name: Freak Fryer
shots.notes: Center tower charged by switch hits (5 levels); maxing it lights Gappa Angry at the House.

shots.name: Pop Bumpers
shots.notes: Three pops in the hidden area behind the house/crypt; pause the Haunt timer while the ball is here.

shots.name: Top Rollover Lanes
shots.notes: Two rollover lanes at the top of the orbit; target of the Dead End top-lane skill shot.

shots.name: Left Inlane
shots.notes: Lower-left return; roll it lit to trigger Double Trouble.

shots.name: Left Outlane
shots.notes: Far lower-left drain; carries the Hand of Fate wheel collect.

shots.name: Right Inlane
shots.notes: Lower-right return; roll it lit to trigger Double Trouble.

shots.name: Right Outlane
shots.notes: Far lower-right drain; carries the RETURN ball-save lit by the 1st Deadhead.

shots.name: Right Slingshot
shots.notes: Slow rollers can drain off this sling; controlled nudge often needed.

shots.name: Shooter Lane / Plunger
shots.notes: Right cabinet edge; auto/manual launch feeds the upper-right orbit/rollovers. Soft-plunge for the Back Door skill shot.

goals.title: Dead End Top-Lane Skill Shot
goals.summary: The safe skill shot: plunge into the lit top rollover lane for points and a +5X bonus multiplier, feeding into the low-risk bumpers.
goals.reward: 250k (+25k each success) plus +5X bonus multiplier

steps.action: Plunge into either Dead End lane
steps.detail: Full or firm plunge feeds the upper hidden area to score and stack +5X bonus; the ball trickles safely on into the pop bumpers afterward. Repeat every ball to pump end-of-ball bonus.

goals.title: Super Secret Back Door Unskilled Shot

goals.reward: 1M base, +250k each (max 2.5M), and qualifies/advances a Haunt

goals.title: Extra Ball via Hand of Fate
goals.summary: Extra Ball is not on the first Hand of Fate wheel, so this is a long path rather than a quick one. Complete the Hand of Fate target bank to light Hand of Fate at the left outlane, then stop the wheel with the lockdown bar action button when a ball drains there. The first wheel holds Ball Save, Extend Garage Multiball, Extend Trunk Multiball, 5 Million, 2 Million and Double Bone-Us; only once all six are collected does a second wheel open, and that is the one carrying Extra Ball.

goals.title: Hand of Fate: Stop the Wheel Yourself
goals.summary: This machine runs a reflex mini-game off a drained ball, and it is easy to mistake for a random consolation prize. Complete the right target bank to light Hand of Fate at the left outlane, and the next ball that drains there puts a spinning wheel on the display — the lockdown bar button, not luck, decides where it stops.
instructions: Complete the right target bank to light HAND OF FATE at the left outlane
Let a ball drain down the lit left outlane instead of trying to save it
Watch for the spinning wheel that appears on the display
Press the lockdown bar action button to stop the wheel on the segment you want
Stop it within 6 seconds — no award is collected if the wheel is not stopped in time
goals.reward: Your pick of six wheel segments: Ball Save, Extend Garage Multiball, Extend Trunk Multiball, 5 Million, 2 Million, or Double Bone-Us. Collect them all and a second wheel opens, with a third after that, and completing every Hand of Fate award starts the Manos Wheel.

drills.title: Soft Plunge The Back Door
drills.text: Ease the plunger so the ball rolls around the top and behind the mansion into the Back Door. It pays real points and hands you a Haunt for free, which is a better opening than anything you can shoot for with a flipper.

drills.title: Front Door Repeats
drills.text: Shoot the House Entrance over and over until the insert flashes purple, then put the next one straight back in to start the Haunt. The ramps do not qualify a Haunt, so this centre shot is the whole spine of the game.

drills.title: Both Ramps, Then Collect
drills.text: The instant a Haunt finishes, take one ramp, then the other, then the House. Collecting straight at the House pays half; the two ramps first are what make it whole, and the hurry-up does not wait for you to decide.

drills.title: Buy Time In The Bumpers
drills.text: Mid-Haunt, put the ball up an orbit into the pop bumpers on purpose. The Haunt clock pauses while it is up there, so learn to spend that trip deliberately instead of only finding the bumpers by accident.

drills.title: One Whole Deadhead
drills.text: Run a full Deadhead without stopping: lower the crypt, wake the skull, batter it down, then come back to the crypt to finish. Every one you beat demands more hits than the last, so the shot has to be repeatable rather than lucky.

drills.title: Orbit, Then Backhand
drills.text: Take the left orbit and backhand the left ramp off the return, then keep the loop going. The crate diverter can carry that same ramp shot on into the Trunk, so one habit builds shot multipliers and lock progress at once.

actionButton.label: Action Button
actionButton.how: Three jobs, all worth knowing. It stops the Hand of Fate wheel on the award you actually want, it fires the Atomic Raygun you pull out of the Trunk, and it aims the Super Head Shot at the Crypt.

uses.when: Ball heading down the lit left outlane
uses.what: Stops the spinning wheel on the display — where it lands is your choice, not luck. No press, no award.

uses.when: Holding the Atomic Raygun from the Trunk
uses.what: Spots a shot in your most recently started Haunt; the button lights in whatever color that shot is.

uses.when: Third Deadhead, Super Head Shot lit
uses.what: Aims at the flashing target at the Crypt — the shot cannot be finished without it.

howItPlays.objective: Elvira is flipping a haunted house, and you restore and sell it by playing through her library of B-movie Haunts. Build your market value across every mode and multiball, then close the sale for the whole accumulated total in Wild Market Value.
loop: Shoot the House entrance until its mansion insert flashes purple, then shoot it again to start a Haunt -- the ramps alone never qualify one.
Play the Haunt out, dipping into the pop bumpers to pause its timer, then cash it at up to full value with both ramps into the House.
Lock balls at the Garage, complete the Trunk targets, and battle the Crypt to run the three standard multiballs, stacking them onto a running Haunt.
Complete the Trunk and Hand of Fate target banks and roll a lit inlane for Double Trouble, then hold 4X so the whole stack is quadrupled.
Finish four Haunts for Director's Cut, tick off all seven requirements, and sell the house at the Cellar.

lights.name: The House & Cellar
lights.lit: Every Haunt begins and ends at the House center, and win one and the front-door steps rise away to expose the Cellar underneath, which closes out many Haunts and is the climax shot for the biggest goals.
lights.flashing: A purple-flashing mansion insert means a Haunt is qualified and the next House shot will start it.
lights.then: Loop the House to qualify and start Haunts, and the moment one finishes take both ramps then the House to bank the full Trailer Trash cash-out. Four completed Haunts light Director's Cut here, and the Cellar is where you eventually sell the house for Wild Market Value.

lights.name: The Garage
lights.lit: Knocking down the gravestone drop guarding the Garage lights its locks; feed three balls in to start Wild Women Multiball, the cheapest multiball to reach and an easy one to layer over a Haunt.
lights.then: Lock three and farm the jackpot ring -- left orbit, ramps, House, right orbit, Crypt -- shooting the House after five jackpots for the Super, which then lights both orbits for supers. Starting Attic Attack, the third Garage multiball, is one of the seven Wild Market Value requirements.

lights.name: Junk in the Trunk
lights.lit: Completing the 36-24-36 standup bank opens the motorized trunk; the left ramp's crate diverter then drops the ball inside to collect a random Junk piece and lock it, and a second lock starts the two-ball Trunk Multiball.
lights.flashing: A flashing trunk insert cycles which of the four collectible Junk items is on offer.
lights.then: Lock through the left ramp and cash its Super Jackpot for one to three Junk pieces. Collecting all four Junk starts Phone-A-Fiend -- another sale requirement -- and pulls out the Atomic Raygun, which the lockdown-bar button fires to spot a shot in your running Haunt.

lights.name: Deadhead Family Crypt
lights.lit: The green crypt is a bash toy: shoot it to lower the mausoleum, wake a Deadhead and batter its skull, then return to the crypt to finish it off, with each successive Deadhead demanding more hits than the last.

control.effect: aim the flashing Super Head Shot at the crypt -- the third Deadhead cannot be finished any other way
control.when: the third Deadhead is up and the Super Head Shot is lit

lights.then: The first Deadhead lights the right-outlane ball save, the second an extra ball, and the third that Super Head Shot, itself one of the seven sale requirements. Defeated heads are held from ball to ball, so no early crypt work is ever wasted.

lights.name: Freak Fryer & Gappa Angry
lights.lit: The center Freak Fryer tower charges on switch hits across five levels; topping it out lights Gappa Angry over at the House, which then runs six escalating lock stages that climb the playfield toward the Cellar.
lights.then: Charge the tower, start at the House, and work the staged locks -- House, then both ramps, then both orbits -- up to the Cellar Super Jackpot and a six-ball multiball. Starting Gappa Angry is another of the seven requirements for the final sale.

lights.name: Double Trouble Playfield X
lights.lit: Complete the Trunk standup bank and the Hand of Fate target bank and one inlane lights for Double Trouble; the lit inlane is what you roll through to switch on playfield-wide multiplier scoring.

control.effect: tap a flipper button to move the lit Double Trouble inlane between the two returns, so the ball rolls through it on the shot you choose
control.when: Double Trouble is lit and the ball is heading for the inlanes

lights.then: Time the lit inlane so it rolls just as a fat scoring window opens and it fires 2X for thirty seconds; re-complete both banks and roll a lit inlane again while it still runs to upgrade to 4X, then work the House and orbit supers with the whole playfield quadrupled.

lights.name: Gar-Goil Targets
lights.lit: The row of green Gar-Goil standups fills the Garg-Oil-Gauge as you complete it; filling the gauge starts Gar-Goils Gone Wild, which turns both orbits into escalating value.
lights.then: Complete the targets to start the mode, then farm the orbits for value that climbs each shot up to a Super Jackpot. Starting Gar-Goils Gone Wild is one of the seven boxes you tick for the final sale.

lights.name: Hand of Fate Wheel
lights.lit: Completing the Hand of Fate target bank arms a spin and lights Hand of Fate at the left outlane; the next ball to drain that way throws a spinning wheel onto the display instead of just dying.

control.effect: press the lockdown-bar button to freeze the wheel wherever you like, so you decide the award rather than leaving it to chance
control.when: the wheel is spinning after a ball drains down the lit left outlane

lights.then: Let a lit-outlane drain feed the wheel and stop it within about six seconds on an award you need -- Double Bone-Us doubles your entire end-of-ball bonus. Collect all six segments and a second wheel opens, which is where the extra ball lives.

howItPlays.laneChangeNote: Complete the Trunk and Hand of Fate target banks and one inlane lights for Double Trouble; tap a flipper button to move the lit inlane between the two returns so the ball rolls through the one you pick. Rolling it fires 2X playfield scoring, and re-qualifying the banks and rolling a lit inlane again while it runs upgrades you to 4X.

scoring.text: Soft-plunge behind the mansion into the Super Secret Back Door for a fat score and a Haunt handed to you free, or take the near-riskless top-lane skill shot for points and a bonus-multiplier bump. Start the Haunt at the House, then dip into the pop bumpers to pause its timer while you learn the shots.

Start a Haunt first, then stack a Garage Multiball on top, since you can pull a multiball into a running Haunt but never start a Haunt once a multiball is going. Pre-bank the Trunk and Hand of Fate targets so you can roll a lit inlane for Double Trouble and hold 4X across the whole stack.

Complete four Haunts for Director's Cut, worth around a hundred million for all four films. Then tick off all seven requirements -- Director's Cut, the Super Head Shot, Phone-A-Fiend, Gappa Angry, Gar-Goils Gone Wild, Attic Attack and They Came From Space -- and sell the house at the Cellar in Wild Market Value, a hurry-up paying your entire accumulated total.
